conviction_note: Nothing found decides this print: a positive peer read (VF/The North Face +4% in the same Jul-Sep quarter, reported 2026-10-28) and a crowded short (17.6% of float) offset a weak consumer backdrop (gasoline peaked $4.48 on 2026-09-21, Michigan sentiment 48) and a name that has fallen after 5 of its last 7 prints, including -5.4% on a Q2 beat-and-raise. So p_up is 48 on an abs move of 8.0, above the 7.34 implied because the October call adds a Q4 guide and a Spring 2027 order-book update. The findings sum to +0.3 and the scaled number is -0.3. Both are close to zero, and the gap in sign is the skew and the reaction history pulling p_up below 50 while the filed facts net slightly positive.
bar: Q3 EPS consensus $1.28 (MarketBeat, 2026-10-22, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-columbia-sportswear-colm-expected-to-post-earnings-on-thursday-2026-10-22/). A second listing quotes $1.25 on 3 estimates. Benzinga's $1.56 is an outlier that looks stale, from before the guide. Revenue consensus is about $942.5-945M. The company guide (Q2 release, 2026-07-30, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050797/000105079726000129/colmfy26q2exhibit991.htm) is net sales $929-943M (down 1.5% to flat vs $943.4M), op margin 8.1-9.5% and EPS $1.15-1.35. FY26: sales $3.43-3.50B (+1-3%, unchanged), op income $290-325M, EPS $4.45-4.90 including about 180bp of IEEPA refund benefit. The revenue consensus sits at or just above the top of the guide, and the EPS consensus sits slightly above the guide midpoint ($1.25). The implied Q4 is $1.094-1.178B, or +2% to +10% on Q4 2025's ~$1.07B.
positioning_check: Short interest was 4,327,124 shares on the 2026-10-15 record date (FINRA publication 2026-10-26), 17.59% of float, 6.4 days to cover, down 1.0% from 4,372,692 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/COLM/short-interest/, fetched 2026-10-29). Float is small because of the large insider holding, so 17.6% of float is a crowded short by this repo's standard. Baseline skew is +4.85 vol points (downside paid), put/call open-interest ratio 10.07 on only 2,259 contracts, and the ATM spread is 53% of mid, so the 7.34% event-implied move is indicative. Run-up is +10.1% over 20 days and +2.3% over 5, with the stock 6.3% off its 52-week high. Quantisnow showed about +4.65% on 2026-10-28 (the VF print day) and about -2.7% intraday 2026-10-29.

findings.finding: VF Corp's quarter covering the same Jul-Sep months (reported 2026-10-28, after Columbia last spoke) showed The North Face, Columbia's closest US outerwear peer, up 4% to about $1.21B. VF's Americas region was +5% in constant currency excluding Dickies, it cited strong orders from wholesale partners, and it beat consensus EPS ($0.70 vs $0.54) and revenue ($2.695B vs $2.667B). That points to an outdoor wholesale channel that took Fall sell-in, against Columbia's guide of a US decline in Q3 and a consensus at the top of its $929-943M range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: COLM sells reported-quarter beats. Q2 2026 beat its revenue guide top ($614M vs $600-610M) and raised FY EPS, and the stock fell 5.43%. Q1 2026 beat ($779M vs ~$756M consensus) and rose +2.35%. Q3 2025 beat revenue ($943M vs $917M) and fell 3.63%. 2 of 7 prints up.
findings.why_not_priced: It is one day old, and COLM's consensus was set before it. Partly priced: COLM showed about +4.65% on 2026-10-28 (quantisnow), which reads as the read-through being bought. If fully priced, the skew would have flattened from +4.85 and consensus revenue would have moved above the guide top. Neither is visible. VF also reaffirmed rather than raised its full year, so the read-through to the guide is weaker than to the quarter.
findings.independence: Benzinga's 2026-10-28 summary gives the same VF numbers (adj EPS $0.70 vs $0.54; TNF +4%; Vans -10%; FY reaffirmed): https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/10/62652255/vf-corp-finds-its-winning-formula-with-north-face-and-timberland-but-vans-lags. Both describe the same VF release. On the Q2 call COLM management said 'no order book changes for fall 2026' and expected North America wholesale growth in H2 (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1949254-20260731).

findings.finding: The bar sits at or above the top of the company's own Q3 revenue guide: consensus is about $945M (MarketBeat) against a guide of $929-943M. EPS consensus is $1.28 against a $1.15-1.35 guide. Columbia has to clear its guide ceiling just to meet the street on sales in a quarter it said would lose more than $30M of Fall shipments to Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Columbia has cleared the top of its revenue guide in recent quarters (Q2 2026 $614.4M vs $600-610M), and the stock still fell 5.43%. A guide-top beat is the expected outcome, not a surprise.
findings.why_not_priced: It is the bar itself, so it is priced by definition. What it adds is that an in-line print against the guide reads as a slight miss against the street. The question is whether the >$30M shift to Q4 (Q2 call) has been fully reflected. Consensus above the guide top suggests analysts expect the usual cushion.
findings.independence: Benzinga's consensus revenue is about $942.5M (search snippet, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/COLM/earnings-forecasts, 403 on fetch), so two estimate sources agree within $3M. The company guide is the primary document.

findings.finding: The US consumer backdrop weakened through the quarter and into Q4. EIA regular gasoline peaked at $4.478 on 2026-09-21 ($4.284 on 10-19), University of Michigan sentiment was 48.0 in October, and Goldman cut 2026 consumption growth to 1.2% on the oil shock. On the Q2 call management named higher fuel prices as weighing on lower- and middle-income consumers, said US brick-and-mortar DTC traffic had softened and stayed flat, Columbia US e-commerce was down low single digits, and it expected more outlet promotion. That threatens Q3 US DTC and the Q4 guide, whose implied range (+2% to +10% Q4 sales) is wide enough to be cut to the low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has driven the reactions. In Q2 2026 the 'H2 incrementally moderated' language and a Q3 guide below consensus brought -5.43% despite an FY EPS raise. Q2 2025 (-12.85%) was also a guidance-led drop.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (late October; cites the EIA 2026-10-19 reading and the final October Michigan index)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the skew of +4.85 and the 10:1 put/call open interest show downside is paid for. But the stock rose 10% over 20 days into the print, which is not what a market expecting a guide cut looks like. Gasoline easing in October (Conference Board confidence rose) is the offset, which is why this is sized small. This is macro-to-company transmission that management confirmed only as a direction in July.
findings.independence: Proxy. Management's own Q2-call language on fuel prices and DTC softness: https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1949254-20260731 (2026-07-31). Conference Board October confidence rose on lower gasoline (cuts the other way): https://gvwire.com/2026/10/27/us-consumer-confidence-improves-in-october/. OIA/Circana Q2 2026 outdoor unit sales fell 5.3% while dollars were flat: https://oia.outdoorindustry.org/q2-2026-outdoor-retail-trends.

findings.finding: Short interest is crowded into the print: 4.33M shares, 17.59% of float, 6.4 days to cover at 2026-10-15, essentially unchanged from 4.37M at 09-30. Puts outnumber calls 10:1 in open interest. A print that is merely in line, with a reassuring Q4/Spring 2027 order-book update, has a squeeze mechanism behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In February 2026 the Q4 print rose +14.44%, the one large up-move in the history, which is the shape a squeeze on a crowded short takes. Otherwise, at lower short interest (6.6% of float in August per equibles), reactions were mostly negative.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, so the question is asymmetry. 17.6% of float is in the range where this repo's resolved shorts squeezed 20%+. Short interest has roughly doubled from the ~3.4M / 6.6% of float that equibles showed in August (different float definitions, so the level is uncertain). If squeeze risk were priced, call skew would be bid. Instead the 25-delta skew is +4.85 toward puts.
findings.independence: equibles' August snapshot of about 3.4M shares (https://equibles.com/stocks/colm/shortinterest) shows the build since the Q2 print, with a different float base. The baseline's put/call OI of 10.07 is a separate measure of the same bearish positioning.

findings.finding: There may be IEEPA refunds Columbia has not yet recognised. CEO Tim Boyle said on Fox Business (2026-05-17) that the company had paid about $90M of IEEPA tariffs, and the Q2 release recognised about $78M of refunds including interest. A residual of up to about $10-15M could land as a one-off in Q3 or later, if the $90M was all IEEPA. That is an inference, not a disclosed receivable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 refund ($0.93 of EPS) was looked through: the stock fell 5.43%. The FY guide already includes about 180bp of refund benefit.
findings.why_not_priced: Not quantified anywhere, and the gap may be other tariffs in the $90M rather than unrefunded IEEPA. The market looked through the first refund, so even a confirmed residual is worth a fraction of its dollars.
findings.independence: Q2 release on the $78M received and the $15M carried in inventory: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050797/000105079726000129/colmfy26q2exhibit991.htm. Same company, different document.

findings.finding: Q3 gross margin carries a guided headwind from 'accommodations to our factory partners', which largely offsets the $15M of IEEPA refund held in inventory, with a net Q4 tailwind. This is inside the Q3 op-margin guide of 8.1-9.5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific to this item. Gross-margin quality has mattered less than the guide on recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is guided and was in the wire, so it is largely priced. It is filed because the size of the accommodation was never quantified, so a gross-margin line below the guide is possible.
findings.independence: The Q2 release states the same Q3 gross-margin pressure: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001050797/000105079726000129/colmfy26q2exhibit991.htm. Shares a source with the guide.

findings.finding: Mountain Hardwear named a new brand president (Peter Rauch) in September 2026, after a $29M prAna/Mountain Hardwear impairment in Q3 2025. It is an emerging-brand management change with no disclosed financial consequence for the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The emerging brands are about 10% of sales. Their impairment in Q3 2025 coincided with a -3.63% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial at group level. Filed for completeness.

outside_window.finding: Section 122 tariffs (10%, Feb-Jul 2026, paid by Columbia) were ruled unlawful by the CIT in May 2026. The ruling is stayed on appeal, and a Federal Circuit decision is projected for late 2026 or early 2027, so any Section 122 refund would be a further one-off after the window.

A proposed class action filed in Oregon federal court in June 2026 accuses Columbia, Columbia Brands and prAna of charging tariff-inflated prices while recovering IEEPA refunds. It has no resolution date in the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: Q3 2026 sell-side previews dated October 2026 with a changed number: none found beyond Wall Street Zen's 10-11 downgrade, Stifel holding Buy/$67 on 10-12, Seaport Neutral 10-20 and BTIG Buy $75 on about 10-15. No estimate-revision trend sourced.

EDGAR since the Q2 8-K: only routine RSU-vest Form 4s (Bragdon 10-01 at $57.69, Luther 09-01 at $56.81, no open-market buys or sells), the 10-Q (08-06) and a 13G (10-08). No 8-K, no buyback disclosure, no executive departure.
September/October 2026 US outerwear sell-through or weather-impact series (Planalytics, OIA VantagePoint monthly): nothing current found.
Deckers/UGG and other outerwear peers reporting in October 2026: no result surfaced. Amer Sports and Canada Goose report after this window.
Status of the Section 122 refund appeal in October 2026: no ruling found.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Benzinga consensus EPS of $1.56 for Q3, which would make the bar far above the company's $1.15-1.35 guide
rejected_candidates.detail: Contradicted by MarketBeat's $1.28 (2026-10-22) and by the company's own guide in the Q2 8-K exhibit. It looks like a stale pre-guide figure, and the page returned 403, so it could not be checked.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Ongoing tariff-rate change: Section 122 expired 2026-07-24 and was replaced by Section 301 'forced labor' duties of 10-12.5%
rejected_candidates.detail: Not a change to Columbia's outlook: the Q2 guide already assumed the 'current 10%-12.5% tariff rates remain in place through the end of this year' (Q2 call). It duplicates the guide's own assumption, so it adds nothing.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The VF read-through and the crowded short cut against the +4.85 put skew, while the macro finding and a 2-of-7 up history agree with it. The +10% 20-day run-up suggests some of the VF read is already in the price, so p_up is held just below 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sells beats, 5 of 7 down including -5.4% on a Q2 beat-and-raise): VF read-through cut +0.6 -> +0.5, held there because 'a peer's print landing after the company last spoke' is the pattern the file says has paid.
Lesson 7 (a crowded short of 17.6% of float shrinks negatives): macro/guidance negative cut -0.8 -> -0.6.
Lesson 2 (one-offs at a fraction, and the Q2 refund was looked through): possible residual IEEPA refund cut +0.2 -> +0.1.

Lesson 6 (bar verified against the company guide and two agreeing estimate sources at $1.25-1.28 / ~$942-945M): no cap needed. The Benzinga $1.56 outlier was rejected. Section 122 refunds and the class action stay in outside_window.
